prediction.likelyOutcome: Franciscan will recover the strip value (roughly $40,500-$47,400) regardless of outcome on the access issue. The case's real value turns on whether the trial court admits the highest-and-best-use/loss-of-access theory over the State's Ensley-based objection and motion in limine; if it does, expect a jury award in the low seven figures anchored closer to the joint appraisers' ~$1.9M figure than to the individual outlier estimates, but there is a substantial chance (perhaps better than even) that the theory is excluded or rejected entirely, leaving Owners with only the strip payment.

issues.label: Loss-of-Access / Highest-and-Best-Use Damages (Ensley vs. Marina Entertainment)

outcome.description: The Johnson Superior Court jury awarded $680,000 to Franciscan and $1.5 million to SCP (a $2.2 million judgment), with attorney's fees awarded to both owners under Ind. Code 32-24-1-14(b) (amount not stated) and 8% prejudgment interest. The Court of Appeals reversed on November 28, 2023, holding the traffic-flow rule bars the access damages, and remanded with instructions to vacate the judgment for SCP and enter judgment for Franciscan for only the value of the strip (appraised at $40,500-$47,400), with prejudgment interest recalculated.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: only the strip taking is compensable, about $40,500-$47,400 on the record; midpoint used.

source.caseName: State of Indiana v. Franciscan Alliance, Inc. f/k/a Sisters of St. Francis Health Services, Inc.; The Market Place at State Road 37, LLC; Hook SupeRX, LLC; SCP 2010-C36-018 LLC; and Johnson County, Indiana
